claims.text: The trip's own telemetry establishes a route deviation under POL-RD-01: the GPS polyline records 11.18 km against a booked optimal of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km or 36.34%, which clears both establishment gates — greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal. The finding rests on the trace figure, which POL-RD-01 makes the governing measurement, not the rounded actual_distance_km.

The route the rider booked carried no ERP at all. trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd is 0.00, and the routing engine's stored optimal is 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials, no gantry'. On the route the rider agreed to, the ERP line would have been zero, so the entire $4.00 of ERP on the bill is a cost the rider's own route never incurred.

Both gantry lines on the bill are CTE gantries the optimal route never uses — the fare breakdown itself marks each on_optimal_route false — and the trace passes the gantry points closely: nearest fix 0.0 m at 08:12:50 for the $3.00 CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) gantry, and 40.2 m at 08:19:40 for the $1.00 CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) gantry. The $4.00 of ERP is therefore the cost of gantries that only the detour, and not the rider's route, crossed.

Even taking the Braddell Road closure as a full exoneration of the detour under POL-RD-03 — as the rider in fact accepts — POL-RD-09(2) still requires off-route ERP to be refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, because the rider did not cause the closure either. The distance and time charges may stand; the $4.00 of CTE ERP does not.

The pass-through correction the rider seeks is $4.00 ($3.00 + $1.00), comfortably within the SGD 12.00 per-trip cap in POL-RD-09(2), so the whole ERP line is refundable and no part of it is barred by that cap.

The detour cannot be attributed to the rider, so POL-RD-09(3) does not bar the ERP refund. The only message proposing the CTE was sent by the DRIVER at 08:12:30 ('braddell close today, i take CTE ah'); the rider's single reply 'ok' is a bare acknowledgement, not a rider instruction. waypoint_hint is null on both messages, so the rider-instruction test in POL-RD-04 cannot be met and the record contains no rider election to cross ERP gantries.

The trace is unbroken — 175 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07, the deviation finding rests on clean telemetry, and there is no gap-based basis for escalation under POL-RD-10(3).

claims.text: The rider clears the POL-RD-08 threshold limb on this trip's own trace — 11.18 km driven against a booked optimal of 8.2 km, an excess of 2.98 km or 36.34% — so the burden shifts to the driver, and the driver discharges it by pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause: the LTA closure advisory ADV-20260714-031. No general assertion that 'traffic was bad' is made or needed.

POL-RD-03 exoneration is made out on all three limbs. (a) The advisory names Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — the arterial the platform's own optimal route uses, recorded as 'Braddell Rd -> Serangoon Rd -> Kallang arterials' with optimal_route_erp_sgd of 0.00. (b) Its validity window of 05:30 to 12:00 overlaps the trip, which ran 08:07 to 08:36, with 35.2 minutes of overlap. (c) The actual route leaves the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoins it after, as the two CTE gantries crossed at 08:14 and 08:19 on a corridor the optimal route never uses show. The advisory text itself sanctions the CTE as one of the two lawful diversions.

The exoneration is capped, and the cap absorbs the whole excess: min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km. The justified excess equals the measured excess, so no residual excess survives on which a POL-RD-02 refund could be founded.

With the whole of the 2.98 km exonerated, POL-RD-02 has nothing left to run on and the driver's meter lines stand in full: base fare SGD 3.80, distance fare SGD 8.40 and time fare SGD 8.12. The rider was not billed for distance that was not driven — 11.2 km charged against 11.18 km on the trace — so no inflated or phantom distance line is concealed in the fare the rider challenges.

The single correction the policy requires — and the ceiling on the rider's recovery — is the off-route ERP. Under POL-RD-09(2) an external-event exoneration leaves distance and time standing but refunds the off-route gantry charges as a standalone pass-through: the two CTE gantries of SGD 3.00 and SGD 1.00, both recorded on_optimal_route false and both matched to the trace well inside the 250 m crossing test (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 40.2 m). That is SGD 4.00, within the SGD 12.00 cap, and under POL-RD-09(1) it is never added on top of any POL-RD-02 figure. The contested SGD 9.00 is therefore not recoverable beyond SGD 4.00.

This is not a MATERIAL deviation, so no POL-RD-06 uplift or conduct referral attaches. The excess of 2.98 km (36.34%) sits below both the 50% and the 8.0 km materiality lines, and the driver_profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 553 — clear of both the 3-flag and the 0.05 ratio tests. No pattern may be built from any other, non-citable profile field.

The chat log independently corroborates the POL-RD-03 reason for the diversion and shows the driver's conduct was transparent, not opportunistic: at 08:12:30, before the first CTE gantry was crossed at 08:14:06, the driver told the rider 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah', and the rider replied 'ok' at 08:12:58. The diversion was driven by the documented closure, and the rider had contemporaneous notice of it.

ruling.explanation: Both sides largely agree on the facts, and the record supports a small refund to the rider. The trip was 11.18 km on the GPS trace against a booked optimal of 8.2 km — an excess of 2.98 km, or 36.3%. That clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 0.8 km and more than 20% of optimal), so a route deviation is established, as both advocates accept. It is not a MATERIAL deviation, because it is below both the 50% line and the 8.0 km line, so no POL-RD-06 conduct review or pattern uplift arises; the driver's profile in any event shows zero deviation flags against 553 completed trips. The deviation is fully excused. LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 records an emergency closure of Braddell Road (towards Serangoon) between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — the very arterial the platform's optimal route uses — from 05:30 to 12:00 on 14 July, overlapping the trip window. The vehicle left that corridor before the closed segment and rejoined it after, taking the CTE exactly as the advisory contemplates. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(2.98, 1.30 × (10.6 − 8.2) + 1.00) = min(2.98, 4.12) = 2.98 km, which absorbs the whole measured excess. The distance and time charges therefore stand, and there is no POL-RD-02 refund on them. What does not stand is the ERP. Because the detour is excused as an external closure, POL-RD-09(2) refunds the off-route gantry charges to the rider: the two CTE gantries of SGD 3.00 (08:14) and SGD 1.00 (08:19), both marked on_optimal_route false and both matched to the trace within 0 m and 40 m respectively — real crossings of a corridor the booked route never used, so no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4) arises. That is SGD 4.00, within the SGD 12.00 per-trip cap. The driver's chat message 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' and the rider's 'ok' show the rider had notice and did not object, but the initiative was the driver's, not a rider instruction, so POL-RD-04 is not engaged and nothing reduces the ERP correction. Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.00; the balance of the contested amount stands. Confidence is high — every artifact relied on carries full weight (1.0) and the trace is unbroken (175 fixes, 10 s interval, no gaps), so no escalation or referral is required.
